te: NBA live dashboard ప్రకారం September 2026 నాటికి Indiaలో 2,76,664 BMCs ఏర్పాటు అయ్యాయి; 2,72,648 PBRs సిద్ధమయ్యాయి. ఇవి permanent figures కావు; ఒక particular dateకు చెందిన administrative totals. ఈ రెండు numbersను కలిపి చూస్తే local system geographical spread ఎంత ఉందో, ఏర్పాటు అయిన committeesలో ఎన్ని అప్పటికి biodiversity registerను సిద్ధం చేశాయో తెలుస్తుంది.

en: By institutional count, the BMC tier—with more than 2.5 lakh committees—is India's largest conservation-governance network. Its number is far above the approximately 1,014 protected areas discussed later in this lesson. This is only a comparison of scale: a local committee and a legally protected geographical area differ in both purpose and legal character.
te: 2.5 లక్షలకు పైగా committees ఉన్నందున, institutional countలో BMC tier Indiaలో largest conservation-governance network. ఈ Lessonలో తరువాత వచ్చే సుమారు 1,014 protected areas countతో పోలిస్తే ఇది చాలా పెద్ద సంఖ్య. కానీ ఇది scale comparison మాత్రమే. Local committee, legally protected geographical area—వాటి purpose, legal character రెండూ వేర్వేరు.

en: The PBR total trails the BMC total by only about four thousand. This close numerical match suggests that most constituted committees were followed by preparation of a local biodiversity register. It points to broad availability of the documentary base needed for benefit-sharing claims, but the numbers alone cannot establish the quality of each PBR.
te: BMC totalతో పోలిస్తే PBR total సుమారు 4,000 మాత్రమే తక్కువ. ఈ రెండు numbers దగ్గరగా ఉండటం వల్ల, చాలా చోట్ల committee ఏర్పడిన తరువాత local biodiversity register కూడా సిద్ధమైందని అర్థమవుతుంది. Benefit-sharing claimsకు అవసరమైన documentary base విస్తృతంగా ఉందని ఇది సూచిస్తుంది. అయితే numbers మాత్రమే ప్రతి PBR qualityని నిర్ధారించలేవు.

en: Wide numerical coverage does not automatically mean high-quality documentation. A PBR may be officially completed but still contain gaps, poorly verified scientific information or entries that are no longer current. The near-equal BMC and PBR totals demonstrate administrative reach; completeness and present accuracy can be judged only by examining the registers themselves.
te: ఎక్కువ సంఖ్యలో PBRs ఉండటం అంటే వాటి documentation quality కూడా తప్పకుండా బాగుందని కాదు. ఒక PBR officially complete అయినప్పటికీ, అందులో gaps ఉండవచ్చు; scientific informationకు సరైన verification లేకపోవచ్చు; entries outdated అయి ఉండవచ్చు. BMC, PBR totals దగ్గరగా ఉండటం administrative reachను చూపుతుంది. Completeness, current accuracy తెలుసుకోవాలంటే registersను స్వయంగా examine చేయాలి.

en: BMC and PBR counts help measure how far India's ABS system has extended to the local level. Because these are date-specific administrative figures rather than timeless facts, they must always be read with their reference date. The September 2026 totals describe implementation only as it stood at that time.
te: India ABS system local levelకు ఎంతవరకు చేరిందో అంచనా వేయడానికి BMC, PBR counts ఉపయోగపడతాయి. ఇవి timeless facts కాకుండా date-specific administrative figures కాబట్టి reference dateతో కలిపే చదవాలి. September 2026 totals, ఆ సమయానికి implementation ఎంతవరకు జరిగిందో మాత్రమే తెలియజేస్తాయి.

en: The Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023 substituted section 37, and the substituted provision came into force on 1 April 2024. The State Biodiversity Board first consults the local body and the BMC concerned and then submits its recommendation. The State Government considers that recommendation and issues the notification; the SBB and BMC do not themselves notify the site.
te: Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023 section 37ను substitute చేసింది; ఆ substituted provision 1 April 2024 నుంచి అమలులోకి వచ్చింది. State Biodiversity Board ముందుగా సంబంధిత local body, BMCతో consultation చేసి recommendation పంపుతుంది. ఆ recommendationను పరిగణించి State Government notification జారీ చేస్తుంది; SBB లేదా BMC స్వయంగా siteను notify చేయవు.

en: Section 37 adds a place-based conservation mechanism—the Biodiversity Heritage Site—to the NBA–SBB–BMC institutional framework. A site may merit recognition because of exceptional species richness, endemism, rare or threatened species, or cultural heritage closely linked to biodiversity. Thus a sacred grove or a landscape conserving a traditional crop landrace may qualify where ecological and cultural values are preserved together.
te: NBA–SBB–BMC institutional frameworkకు section 37 ఒక place-based conservation mechanismను జోడిస్తుంది; అదే Biodiversity Heritage Site (BHS). Exceptional species richness, endemism, rare లేదా threatened species, biodiversityతో దగ్గరగా ముడిపడిన cultural heritage వంటి విలువల వల్ల ఒక siteకు recognition రావచ్చు. అందుకే sacred grove లేదా traditional crop landraceను కాపాడే landscapeలో ecological, cultural values రెండూ ఉంటే అది qualify కావచ్చు.

en: Formal power to notify a Biodiversity Heritage Site belongs only to the State Government. The 2023 Amendment, however, replaced section 37(1) and altered the procedure that must occur before notification. Since older study material may still describe the earlier process, examination answers should follow the current statutory text.
te: Biodiversity Heritage Siteను formally notify చేసే power State Governmentకు మాత్రమే ఉంది. అయితే 2023 Amendment, section 37(1)ను replace చేసి notificationకు ముందు పాటించాల్సిన procedureను మార్చింది. Older study materialలో పాత process కనిపించవచ్చు. Exam answer మాత్రం current statutory text ప్రకారమే ఉండాలి.

en: Amended section 37 assigns three separate legal functions to different actors. The local body and BMC are consulted; the SBB considers that consultation and recommends the site; the State Government issues the Gazette notification. Consultation, recommendation and notification should therefore never be treated as interchangeable steps.
te: Amended section 37 మూడు separate legal functionsను వేర్వేరు actorsకు ఇచ్చింది. Local body, BMCతో consultation జరుగుతుంది; దాన్ని పరిగణనలోకి తీసుకుని SBB siteను recommend చేస్తుంది; State Government Gazette notificationను issue చేస్తుంది. కాబట్టి consultation, recommendation, notificationను ఒకే stepగా భావించకూడదు.

en: An SBB recommendation is now a compulsory legal condition for notification. The State Government cannot complete a BHS notification without that recommendation. The proviso also gives the BMC an express role: before recommending the site, the SBB must consult both the relevant local body and the BMC.
te: BHS notificationకు SBB recommendation ఇప్పుడు compulsory legal condition. ఆ recommendation లేకుండా State Government notificationను complete చేయలేదు. Proviso, BMCకి కూడా express role ఇచ్చింది. Siteను recommend చేసే ముందు SBB, relevant local bodyతో పాటు BMCతో కూడా తప్పనిసరిగా consult చేయాలి.

en: An SBB recommendation is now a compulsory legal condition for notification. The State Government cannot complete a BHS notification without that recommendation. en: The State Government retains the final notifying authority. The SBB may recommend and the BMC must be consulted, but neither can issue the BHS notification. In practice, the People's Biodiversity Register maintained by the BMC can supply local evidence of a site's biodiversity value and support its consideration by higher-level bodies.
te: Final notification authority State Governmentకే ఉంటుంది. SBB recommend చేస్తుంది; BMCతో consultation జరుగుతుంది; కానీ ఈ రెండింటిలో ఏ body కూడా BHS notificationను issue చేయలేదు. Practicalగా, BMC maintain చేసే People's Biodiversity Register site biodiversity valueకు local evidenceను అందించి, higher-level considerationకు support ఇవ్వగలదు.

en: In September 2026, the NBA live dashboard listed 57 notified Biodiversity Heritage Sites. The WII–ENVIS database had listed 54 sites in 17 states in January 2024, while still older material reported 44. These figures are not mutually inconsistent: each is a dated snapshot of a network that expands whenever another site is notified.
te: NBA live dashboardలో September 2026 నాటికి 57 notified Biodiversity Heritage Sites కనిపించాయి. WII–ENVIS database January 2024 నాటికి 17 Statesలో 54 sitesను చూపింది; మరింత పాత materialలో 44 అనే figure ఉంది. ఇవి పరస్పరం conflict అయ్యే totals కావు. కొత్త sites notify అవుతున్నకొద్దీ పెరిగే networkకు సంబంధించిన different dated snapshots.

en: The national BHS total changes each time a State Government notifies a new site. More broadly, the BDA places the NBA at national level, SBBs at state level and BMCs at local-body level. Calling this arrangement a three-tier system refers to coordination across levels, not an administrative chain of command. A BMC is constituted by its local body; it is not an SBB field office.
te: State Government కొత్త siteను notify చేసినప్పుడల్లా national BHS total మారుతుంది. BDA structureలో national levelలో NBA, State levelలో SBBs, local-body levelలో BMCs ఉంటాయి. దీనిని three-tier system అనడం levels మధ్య coordinationను సూచిస్తుంది; administrative chain of commandను కాదు. BMCని దాని local body ఏర్పాటు చేస్తుంది; అది SBB field office కాదు.

en: Under amended section 41(1), responsibility for constituting a BMC rests with the local body itself. In a rural area, this is the Gram Panchayat; in an urban area, it is the specified Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Committee or Municipal Corporation. The SBB neither creates the BMC nor appoints or removes its members.
te: Amended section 41(1) ప్రకారం BMCని constitute చేసే బాధ్యత local bodyకే ఉంది. Rural areaలో Gram Panchayat; urban areaలో specified Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Committee లేదా Municipal Corporation ఈ పని చేస్తాయి. SBB, BMCని create చేయదు; దాని membersను appoint చేయదు లేదా remove చేయదు.

en: Each of the three institutions is created by a different authority. Section 8 empowers the Central Government to establish the NBA; section 22 assigns establishment of an SBB to the State Government; and section 41 requires the local body to constitute its BMC. None is merely a branch office of the body placed above it in the three-level arrangement.
te: ఈ మూడు institutionsను different authorities ఏర్పాటు చేస్తాయి. Section 8 కింద Central Government NBAను establish చేస్తుంది; section 22 కింద State Government SBBను establish చేస్తుంది; section 41 కింద local body తన BMCని constitute చేస్తుంది. Three-level arrangementలో ఒక body, దాని పై level bodyకి mere branch office కాదు.

en: A BMC is accountable chiefly within its local-government framework, not through a departmental hierarchy leading to the SBB. The PBR is a local record maintained by the committee, not a routine return submitted to the Board. Section 37 further confirms this distinct local role by requiring the SBB to consult the BMC before it recommends a BHS.
te: BMC ప్రధానంగా తన local-government frameworkలో accountableగా ఉంటుంది; SBBకు వెళ్లే departmental hierarchyలో కాదు. PBR అనేది committee maintain చేసే local record; Boardకు పంపే routine return కాదు. BHS recommendationకు ముందు SBB, BMCతో consult చేయాలని section 37 చెప్పడం కూడా BMC distinct local roleను confirm చేస్తుంది.

en: It is wrong to call BMCs the field units of SBBs or to claim that an SBB creates village-level committees. The Central Government establishes the NBA, the State Government establishes the SBB, and the relevant local body constitutes the BMC.
te: BMCలను SBB field unitsగా చెప్పడం, village-level BMCలను SBB ఏర్పాటు చేస్తుందని చెప్పడం తప్పు. Central Government NBAను establish చేస్తుంది; State Government SBBను establish చేస్తుంది; relevant local body BMCని constitute చేస్తుంది.

en: The 2023 Amendment, effective from 1 April 2024, replaced criminal punishment for the relevant BDA contraventions with monetary penalties imposed through adjudication. The ordinary range under the 2024 Rules is ₹1 lakh to ₹50 lakh. Where assessed damage is higher, the penalty may be fixed at a commensurate amount; failure or a continuing contravention can attract an additional penalty of up to ₹1 crore. Any liability arising under another applicable law remains unaffected.
te: 1 April 2024 నుంచి effective అయిన 2023 Amendment, relevant BDA contraventionsకు ఉన్న criminal punishment స్థానంలో adjudication ద్వారా monetary penaltiesను తీసుకొచ్చింది. 2024 Rules కింద ordinary penalty range ₹1 lakh నుంచి ₹50 lakh. Assessed damage దీనికంటే ఎక్కువైతే, damageకు commensurate amountను penaltyగా నిర్ణయించవచ్చు. Failure లేదా continuing contraventionకు additional penalty ₹1 crore వరకు ఉండవచ్చు. మరో applicable law కింద వచ్చే liability మాత్రం అలాగే కొనసాగుతుంది.

en: The 2023 Amendment, effective from 1 April 2024, replaced criminal punishment for the relevant BDA contraventions with monetary penalties imposed through adjudication. The ordinary range under the 2024 Rules is ₹1 lakh to ₹50 lakh. Where assessed damage is higher, the penalty may be fixed at a commensurate amount; failure or a continuing contravention can attract an additional penalty of up to ₹1 crore. Any liability arising under another applicable law remains unaffected.
te: 1 April 2024 నుంచి effective అయిన 2023 Amendment, relevant BDA contraventionsకు ఉన్న criminal punishment స్థానంలో adjudication ద్వారా monetary penaltiesను తీసుకొచ్చింది. 2024 Rules కింద ordinary penalty range ₹1 lakh నుంచి ₹50 lakh. Assessed damage దీనికంటే ఎక్కువైతే, damageకు commensurate amountను penaltyగా నిర్ణయించవచ్చు. Failure లేదా continuing contraventionకు additional penalty ₹1 crore వరకు ఉండవచ్చు. మరో applicable law కింద వచ్చే liability మాత్రం అలాగే కొనసాగుతుంది.

en: The exclusions must be read narrowly from amended section 7. They cover codified traditional knowledge; cultivated medicinal plants and their products; specified local people and communities; growers and cultivators; and vaids, hakims and registered AYUSH practitioners who practise indigenous medicine for sustenance and livelihood. They do not create a blanket exemption for every AYUSH enterprise, use of wild biological resources or foreign-linked person. Amended section 6 separately moves the relevant IP trigger from filing an application to grant of the right.
te: Amended section 7లోని exclusionsను narrowగానే చదవాలి. Codified traditional knowledge; cultivated medicinal plants, వాటి products; specified local people, communities; growers, cultivators; sustenance, livelihood కోసం indigenous medicine practice చేసే vaids, hakims, registered AYUSH practitioners వీటి పరిధిలోకి వస్తారు. కానీ every AYUSH enterprise, wild biological resources use లేదా foreign-linked personకు blanket exemption లేదు. వేరుగా, amended section 6లో relevant IP trigger application filing నుంచి right grant దశకు మారింది.

en: Under substituted section 6, the decisive stage is grant of the IP right rather than filing of the application. This change in timing applies to both Indian and foreign applicants. Their legal routes still differ, because each category must fulfil a different obligation at or before that stage.
te: Substituted section 6 ప్రకారం decisive stage IP application filing కాదు; IP right grant. ఈ timing change Indian, foreign applicants ఇద్దరికీ వర్తిస్తుంది. అయినప్పటికీ వారి legal routes వేరు, ఎందుకంటే ఆ stageలో లేదా దానికి ముందు ప్రతి category fulfil చేయాల్సిన obligation వేరుగా ఉంటుంది.

en: A foreign-linked person or entity falling under section 3(2) must secure prior approval from the NBA before the IP right is granted. The 2023 Amendment shifted the trigger from application filing to grant, but it did not replace prior approval with simple registration for this category.
te: Section 3(2) పరిధిలోకి వచ్చే foreign-linked person లేదా entity, IP right grantకు ముందు NBA prior approval తప్పనిసరిగా పొందాలి. 2023 Amendment triggerను application filing నుంచి grantకు మార్చింది. కానీ ఈ categoryకి prior approval స్థానంలో simple registrationను పెట్టలేదు.

en: A foreign-linked person or entity falling under section 3(2) must secure prior approval from the NBA before the IP right is granted. The 2023 Amendment shifted the trigger from application filing to grant, but it did not replace prior approval with simple registration for this category.
te: Section 3(2) పరిధిలోకి వచ్చే foreign-linked person లేదా entity, IP right grantకు ముందు NBA prior approval తప్పనిసరిగా పొందాలి. 2023 Amendment triggerను application filing నుంచి grantకు మార్చింది. కానీ ఈ categoryకి prior approval స్థానంలో simple registrationను పెట్టలేదు.

en: A section 7 Indian person must complete two distinct steps. Section 6(1A) requires registration with the NBA before the IP right is granted, and section 6(1B) requires NBA prior approval when that right is commercialised. Approval has therefore been deferred to commercialisation, not removed altogether.
te: Section 7 పరిధిలోని Indian person రెండు separate steps complete చేయాలి. Section 6(1A) ప్రకారం IP right grantకు ముందు NBAతో registration చేయాలి. Section 6(1B) ప్రకారం ఆ rightను commercialise చేసే సమయంలో NBA prior approval పొందాలి. అందువల్ల approval remove కాలేదు; commercialisation stageకు defer అయింది.

en: A section 7 Indian person must complete two distinct steps. Section 6(1B) ప్రకారం ఆ rightను commercialise చేసే సమయంలో NBA prior approval పొందాలి. అందువల్ల approval remove కాలేదు; commercialisation stageకు defer అయింది.

en: The Amendment replaced the expression 'by-products' with the defined term 'derivative'. A derivative is a naturally occurring biochemical compound produced through the genetic expression or metabolism of biological or genetic resources, whether or not it contains functional units of heredity. This language more closely follows Nagoya Protocol terminology, but the Act and applicable rules must still be applied to decide whether a particular material falls within ABS.
te: Amendment, ‘by-products’ అనే expression స్థానంలో defined term ‘derivative’ను ఉపయోగించింది. Biological లేదా genetic resourcesలో genetic expression లేదా metabolism వల్ల naturally ఏర్పడే biochemical compoundను derivative అంటారు. అందులో functional units of heredity ఉన్నా లేకపోయినా definition వర్తించవచ్చు. ఈ language Nagoya Protocol terminologyకి మరింత దగ్గరగా ఉంది. అయితే particular materialకు ABS వర్తిస్తుందా అనే నిర్ణయం Act, applicable Rules ఆధారంగానే తీసుకోవాలి.

A derivative is a naturally occurring biochemical compound produced through the genetic expression or metabolism of biological or genetic resources, whether or not it contains functional units of heredity. en: The Government describes the 2023 changes as a way to remove unnecessary compliance obstacles affecting research, patenting and AYUSH activity based on Indian biological resources. It points to the later increase in related patent applications as evidence that participation became easier. This is the Government's assessment of policy impact, not a proposition stated in the statutory text.
te: Government వివరణ ప్రకారం 2023 changes, Indian biological resources ఆధారంగా జరిగే research, patenting, AYUSH activityలో unnecessary compliance obstaclesను తగ్గించాయి. తరువాత related patent applications పెరగడాన్ని participation సులభమైందనే evidenceగా Government చూపుతోంది. ఇది statutory textలో ఉన్న proposition కాదు; policy impactపై Government assessment.

en: Critics draw attention to another possible effect. Under the amended arrangement, the NBA has a larger role in negotiating ABS on behalf of local communities, instead of the communities directly helping to settle every benefit-sharing term. Their concern is that simpler compliance may weaken part of the Act's objective of empowering communities.
te: Critics మరో possible effectను గుర్తిస్తున్నారు. ప్రతి benefit-sharing termను settle చేయడంలో local communities directగా పాల్గొనడం బదులు, వారి behalfపై ABS negotiate చేసే NBA role amended arrangementలో పెరిగింది. Compliance సులభమైనా, communitiesను empower చేయాలనే Act objectiveలో ఒక భాగం weaken కావచ్చనేది వారి concern.

en: Supporters and critics are evaluating the same amendment from different policy perspectives. Supporters stress easier compliance, whereas critics stress the possible loss of direct community participation. Neither assessment is the wording of the statute itself. The AYUSH-related exclusion introduced by the amendment remains limited and conditional.
te: Supporters, critics ఒకే Amendmentను different policy perspectives నుంచి evaluate చేస్తున్నారు. Supporters easier complianceను emphasise చేస్తే, critics direct community participation తగ్గే possibilityని emphasise చేస్తున్నారు. ఈ రెండు assessmentsలో ఏదీ statute wording కాదు. Amendment తీసుకొచ్చిన AYUSH-related exclusion limitedగా, conditionsతోనే ఉంటుంది.

Amendment తీసుకొచ్చిన AYUSH-related exclusion limitedగా, conditionsతోనే ఉంటుంది.

en: The AYUSH-related exemption is confined to cultivated medicinal plants and their products where the knowledge used has already been codified in the prescribed authoritative texts. It does not extend to commercial bioprospecting involving wild-harvested resources, cancel the ABS obligations of foreign entities, or remove the NBA from the regulatory system.
te: AYUSH-related exemption, prescribed authoritative textsలో ఇప్పటికే codify అయిన knowledge ఆధారంగా ఉపయోగించే cultivated medicinal plants, వాటి productsకే పరిమితం. Wild-harvested resourcesతో జరిగే commercial bioprospectingకు ఇది వర్తించదు. Foreign entities ABS obligationsను cancel చేయదు; regulatory systemలో NBA roleను కూడా remove చేయదు.

en: The 2023 Amendment did not end benefit sharing. It created only limited, conditional exclusions, while the wider ABS framework continued. That framework includes National, State and Local Biodiversity Funds, each with legally specified receipts and permitted uses.
te: 2023 Amendment benefit sharingను end చేయలేదు. Limited, conditional exclusions మాత్రమే ఇచ్చింది; wider ABS framework కొనసాగుతోంది. ఇందులో National, State, Local Biodiversity Funds ఉంటాయి. ప్రతి Fundలో ఏ receipts చేరాలి, వాటిని ఏ purposesకు use చేయాలి అనేది law చెబుతుంది.

en: The 2023 Amendment did not end benefit sharing. It created only limited, conditional exclusions, while the wider ABS framework continued. That framework includes National, State and Local Biodiversity Funds, each with legally specified receipts and permitted uses.
te: 2023 Amendment benefit sharingను end చేయలేదు. Limited, conditional exclusions మాత్రమే ఇచ్చింది; wider ABS framework కొనసాగుతోంది. ఇందులో National, State, Local Biodiversity Funds ఉంటాయి. ప్రతి Fundలో ఏ receipts చేరాలి, వాటిని ఏ purposesకు use చేయాలి అనేది law చెబుతుంది.

en: The three Biodiversity Funds correspond to the national, state and local levels, but three questions must be answered separately for each fund: which section creates it, which receipts enter it, and what expenditure the Act permits.
te: Three Biodiversity Funds national, State, local levelsకు correspond అవుతాయి. ప్రతి Fund గురించి మూడు questionsను separateగా చూడాలి: ఏ section దాన్ని create చేసింది? ఏ receipts అందులో చేరతాయి? Act ఏ expenditureను permit చేస్తుంది?

en: The three Biodiversity Funds correspond to the national, state and local levels, but three questions must be answered separately for each fund: which section creates it, which receipts enter it, and what expenditure the Act permits.
te: Three Biodiversity Funds national, State, local levelsకు correspond అవుతాయి. ప్రతి Fund గురించి మూడు questionsను separateగా చూడాలి: ఏ section దాన్ని create చేసింది? ఏ receipts అందులో చేరతాయి? Act ఏ expenditureను permit చేస్తుంది?

en: Section 27 creates the National Biodiversity Fund. It receives section 26 grants and loans, NBA charges and benefit-sharing amounts, and other Central Government-specified sums. It may pay benefit claimers and support conservation, source-area development and locally consulted socio-economic development.
te: Section 27 National Biodiversity Fundను create చేస్తుంది. Section 26 grants and loans, NBA collect చేసే charges, benefit-sharing amounts, Central Government specify చేసే other sums ఇందులో చేరతాయి. Benefit claimersకు payment, conservation, source-area development, local bodiesతో consultation ద్వారా socio-economic developmentకు దీనిని use చేయవచ్చు.

en: Section 32 establishes the State Biodiversity Fund. Its receipts include State grants and loans, NBA allocations and SBB charges or benefit-sharing amounts. It supports conservation, sustainable use, source-area development, BHS management, and compensation or rehabilitation of people economically affected by a BHS notification.
te: Section 32 State Biodiversity Fundను establish చేస్తుంది. State grants and loans, NBA allocations, SBB charges లేదా benefit-sharing amounts ఇందులో చేరతాయి. Conservation, sustainable use, source-area development, BHS management, అలాగే BHS notification వల్ల economically affected peopleకు compensation లేదా rehabilitation కోసం Fundను use చేయవచ్చు.

en: Section 43 creates the Local Biodiversity Fund, and section 44 governs its use. Government or biodiversity-authority grants and loans, section 41(3) BMC access fees and benefit-sharing receipts enter it. Spending must serve biodiversity and the local community within that local body’s jurisdiction.
te: Section 43 Local Biodiversity Fundను create చేస్తుంది; section 44 దాని useను govern చేస్తుంది. Government లేదా biodiversity-authority grants and loans, section 41(3) BMC access fees, benefit-sharing receipts ఇందులో చేరతాయి. Spending ఆ local body jurisdictionలో biodiversity, local community benefitకే ఉండాలి.

Spending must serve biodiversity and the local community within that local body’s jurisdiction.

Government లేదా biodiversity-authority grants and loans, section 41(3) BMC access fees, benefit-sharing receipts ఇందులో చేరతాయి. Spending ఆ local body jurisdictionలో biodiversity, local community benefitకే ఉండాలి.

en: These Funds show that the BDA controls access and also creates channels for sharing benefits. ABS receipts can move lawfully through national, state and local funds and reach eligible benefit claimers.
te: ఈ Funds వల్ల BDA accessను control చేయడమే కాక benefitsను share చేసే channelsను కూడా create చేస్తుంది. ABS receipts national, State, local Funds ద్వారా legally flow అయి eligible benefit claimersకు చేరవచ్చు.

en: Permitted expenditure becomes progressively more local. The National Fund channels benefits and supports source areas; the State Fund additionally supports BHS management and affected people; the Local Fund is confined to biodiversity and community benefit within its own jurisdiction.
te: National నుంచి local levelకు వచ్చేకొద్దీ permitted expenditure మరింత local-specific అవుతుంది. National Fund benefits, source areasకు support ఇస్తుంది. State Fund BHS management, affected peopleను కూడా cover చేస్తుంది. Local Fund తన jurisdictionలో biodiversity, community benefitకే limited.

en: This pattern reflects subsidiarity: where suitable, decisions and money should be handled close to the resource and community. The same principle connects NBA, SBB and BMC functions, but it creates coordination rather than an administrative command chain.
te: ఈ pattern subsidiarity principleను చూపుతుంది: suitableగా ఉన్నప్పుడు decisions, moneyను resource, communityకు close levelలో handle చేయాలి. ఇదే principle NBA, SBB, BMC functionsను connect చేస్తుంది; కానీ administrative command chainను create చేయదు.

en: Three dates must be separated for the Biological Diversity Rules, 2024: signature on 22 October, Gazette publication on 25 October, and commencement on 24 December 2024 after sixty days. A separate procedural amendment followed on 6 May 2025.
te: Biological Diversity Rules, 2024కు three datesను mix చేయకూడదు: 22 October signature; 25 October Gazette publication; sixty days తరువాత 24 December 2024 commencement. Separate procedural amendment 6 May 2025న వచ్చింది.

en: The Biological Diversity Amendment Rules were separately notified on 6 May 2025. This date is not the signature, publication or commencement date of the principal 2024 Rules. The official Gazette distinguishes the instruments and their G.S.R. notifications.
te: Biological Diversity Amendment Rulesను separateగా 6 May 2025న notify చేశారు. ఈ date principal 2024 Rules signature, publication లేదా commencement date కాదు. Official Gazette instrumentsను, వాటి G.S.R. notificationsను clearly separate చేస్తుంది.

en: MoEFCC made the principal Rules under BDA section 62 through G.S.R. 665(E). The instrument was signed on 22 October 2024, but signing alone did not determine commencement because the Rules linked operation to Gazette notification.
te: BDA section 62 powerతో MoEFCC principal Rulesను G.S.R. 665(E)గా చేసింది. Instrument 22 October 2024న sign అయింది. కానీ Rules operationను Gazette notificationతో link చేసినందున signature alone commencementను determine చేయదు.

en: The controlling Gazette is the Gazette of India Extraordinary, Part II, section 3(i), No. 607, with masthead date 25 October 2024 and ID CG-DL-E-25102024-258244. Thus 25 October is the publication date, not 22 October.

en: Rule 1(2) provides commencement sixty days after Official Gazette notification. Counting from the 25 October 2024 publication gives 24 December 2024 as the commencement date; 22 October remains only the signature date.

en: The apparent three-day discrepancy arises when the 22 October signature date is mistaken for the 25 October publication date. Because the sixty-day period runs from Gazette notification, using the wrong starting date produces the wrong commencement date.

en: A rule may be signed and Gazette-published on different dates. When its commencement clause refers to Gazette notification, publication controls the calculation. The BDA and 2023 Amendment provide the statutory framework; the 2024 Rules provide the detailed process from their commencement.

en: Do not combine two separate reforms. From 1 April 2024, the 2023 Amendment replaced the relevant BDA imprisonment provisions with monetary adjudication. Amended section 6 also requires a section 3(2) applicant to obtain NBA approval before IP grant rather than before application filing.

en: A section 7 Indian applicant follows two distinct IP steps: NBA registration before grant under section 6(1A), and NBA prior approval at commercialisation under section 6(1B). Separately, the Amendment provides only specified exclusions connected with cultivated medicinal plants and codified knowledge.

en: The Act creates National, State and Local Biodiversity Funds. The National Fund channels benefits and supports source areas; the State Fund also covers BHS management and affected people; the Local Fund uses receipts, including BMC fees, for biodiversity within its jurisdiction. Purpose becomes more local at each lower level.
te: Act National, State, Local Biodiversity Fundsను create చేస్తుంది. National Fund benefitsను channel చేసి source areasకు support ఇస్తుంది. State Fund BHS management, affected peopleను కూడా cover చేస్తుంది. Local Fund BMC feesతో సహా receiptsను తన jurisdiction biodiversity కోసం use చేస్తుంది. Lower levelకు వెళ్లేకొద్దీ purpose మరింత local అవుతుంది.

en: The BDA framework consists of the NBA, SBBs and local BMCs that maintain PBRs. The 2023 Amendment introduced monetary penalties and limited exclusions. Section 7 applicants register before IP grant and seek approval at commercialisation; section 3(2) applicants need approval before grant. The 2024 Rules were notified as G.S.R. 665(E).
te: BDA frameworkలో NBA, SBBs, PBRలను maintain చేసే local BMCs ఉన్నాయి. 2023 Amendment monetary penalties, limited exclusionsను తీసుకొచ్చింది. Section 7 applicants IP grantకు ముందు register చేసి commercialisationలో approval పొందాలి; section 3(2) applicants grantకు ముందు approval పొందాలి. 2024 Rules G.S.R. 665(E)గా notify అయ్యాయి.

en: Rule 1(2) brought the Rules into force sixty days after Gazette notification. Publication on 25 October therefore yields 24 December 2024 as commencement. A separate minor amendment was issued on 6 May 2025.
te: Rule 1(2) ప్రకారం Gazette notification తరువాత sixty daysకు Rules అమల్లోకి వచ్చాయి. 25 October publication ఆధారంగా commencement 24 December 2024. Separate minor amendment 6 May 2025న issue అయింది.

en: Under amended section 37, the State Government may notify a BHS only on an SBB recommendation. Before recommending, the SBB must consult both the relevant local body and BMC. Consultation, recommendation and notification therefore belong to different actors.
te: Amended section 37 ప్రకారం SBB recommendationపై మాత్రమే State Government BHSను notify చేయగలదు. Recommendationకు ముందు SBB relevant local body, BMC రెండింటితో consult చేయాలి. Consultation, recommendation, notification మూడు వేర్వేరు actorsకు చెందిన functions.

en: After the amendment, an SBB recommendation and prior consultation with both the local body and BMC are statutory steps; only the State Government notifies. The September 2026 NBA dashboard figure of 57 BHSs is a dated snapshot, while 44 and the January 2024 WII–ENVIS figure of 54 are older snapshots. A BMC is not subordinate to an SBB.
te: Amendment తరువాత SBB recommendation, local bodyతో పాటు BMC consultation statutory steps; State Government మాత్రమే notify చేస్తుంది. September 2026 NBA dashboardలో 57 BHSs అనేది dated snapshot; 44, January 2024 WII–ENVIS 54 older snapshots. BMC, SBBకు subordinate కాదు.

en: Different authorities constitute the three bodies. The Central Government establishes the NBA under section 8, the State Government establishes the SBB under section 22, and the relevant rural or urban local body constitutes the BMC under section 41(1).
te: Three bodiesను different authorities constitute చేస్తాయి. Section 8 కింద Central Government NBAను, section 22 కింద State Government SBBను, section 41(1) కింద relevant rural లేదా urban local body BMCని constitute చేస్తుంది.

en: The institutional pyramid represents coordination and reporting, not command. The September 2026 NBA dashboard listed 2,76,664 BMCs and 2,72,648 PBRs, making this the largest Indian conservation-governance network by institutional count. The totals indicate reach, not the quality of every register.

en: Turmeric wound-healing, neem pesticidal and basmati name or trait claims became major biopiracy disputes before India had a domestic ABS law. India challenged them through legal and diplomatic routes. India ratified the CBD in 1994 and enacted the BDA in 2002; the 1990s disputes increased the political urgency for legislation.
te: Turmeric wound-healing, neem pesticidal, basmati name లేదా trait claims domestic ABS lawకు ముందు major biopiracy disputes అయ్యాయి. India వాటిని legal, diplomatic routesలో challenge చేసింది. India 1994లో CBD ratify చేసి, 2002లో BDA enact చేసింది; 1990s disputes legislation urgencyని పెంచాయి.

en: Benefit sharing was not abolished by the 2023 Amendment. It introduced only specified exclusions associated with cultivated medicinal plants, codified traditional knowledge and eligible actors. Foreign-linked ABS duties and the NBA’s broader statutory role continue.
te: 2023 Amendment benefit sharingను abolish చేయలేదు. Cultivated medicinal plants, codified traditional knowledge, eligible actorsకు సంబంధించిన specified exclusions మాత్రమే ఇచ్చింది. Foreign-linked ABS duties, NBA broader statutory role కొనసాగుతాయి.

en: The move from IP filing to grant was not confined to Indian applicants. Substituted section 6 uses grant as the relevant stage for both Indian and foreign-linked applicants; the difference lies in whether registration or prior approval is required and when commercialisation approval applies.
te: IP filing నుంచి grantకు shift Indian applicantsకే limited కాదు. Substituted section 6లో Indian, foreign-linked applicants ఇద్దరికీ grant relevant stage. Difference registrationనా, prior approvalనా, commercialisation approval ఎప్పుడు అవసరమా అన్న obligationలో ఉంటుంది.

en: Section 3(2) applicants require NBA prior approval before grant under section 6(1). Section 7 Indian applicants register before grant under section 6(1A) and obtain prior approval at commercialisation under section 6(1B). This second step means the Indian route is not approval-free.
te: Section 3(2) applicants section 6(1) కింద grantకు ముందు NBA prior approval పొందాలి. Section 7 Indian applicants section 6(1A) కింద grantకు ముందు register చేసి, section 6(1B) కింద commercialisationలో prior approval పొందాలి. ఈ second step వల్ల Indian route approval-free కాదు.

en: An Indian section 7 applicant is not wholly exempt from NBA approval. Section 6(1A) requires registration before grant, while section 6(1B) still requires prior approval when the resulting IP right is commercialised.
te: Indian section 7 applicantకు NBA approval నుంచి complete exemption లేదు. Section 6(1A) grantకు ముందు registration కోరుతుంది; resulting IP right commercialise చేసే సమయంలో section 6(1B) prior approval ఇంకా అవసరం.

en: For section 7 applicants, section 6(1B) postpones approval to commercialisation; it does not remove it. Do not confuse this IP rule with BHS procedure: under section 37 the SBB recommends after consultation, and only the State Government notifies.
te: Section 7 applicantsకు section 6(1B) approvalను commercialisation వరకు postpone చేస్తుంది; remove చేయదు. ఈ IP ruleను BHS procedureతో mix చేయకూడదు. Section 37 కింద consultation తరువాత SBB recommend చేస్తుంది; State Government మాత్రమే notify చేస్తుంది.

en: The State Government cannot bypass amended section 37(1). The SBB must first consult the relevant local body and BMC and then recommend the site; only afterwards may the State Government notify it. The legal order is consultation, recommendation, notification.
te: State Government amended section 37(1)ను bypass చేయలేదు. SBB ముందుగా relevant local body, BMCతో consult చేసి siteను recommend చేయాలి; తరువాత మాత్రమే State Government notify చేయగలదు. Legal order: consultation, recommendation, notification.

en: The State Government cannot bypass amended section 37(1). The SBB must first consult the relevant local body and BMC and then recommend the site; only afterwards may the State Government notify it. The legal order is consultation, recommendation, notification.
te: State Government amended section 37(1)ను bypass చేయలేదు. SBB ముందుగా relevant local body, BMCతో consult చేసి siteను recommend చేయాలి; తరువాత మాత్రమే State Government notify చేయగలదు. Legal order: consultation, recommendation, notification.

en: The claim that a BMC has no formal section 37 role relies on the old provision. The substituted section expressly requires consultation with both the local body and BMC before an SBB recommends a BHS. Omitting BMC consultation now omits a statutory step.
te: BMCకు section 37లో formal role లేదనే claim old provisionపై ఆధారపడింది. Substituted section ప్రకారం SBB BHS recommend చేయడానికి ముందు local body, BMC రెండింటితో expressly consult చేయాలి. BMC consultation omit చేస్తే statutory step miss అవుతుంది.

en: BMCs are not village field units of an SBB. Section 8 assigns NBA establishment to the Central Government, section 22 assigns SBB establishment to the State Government, and section 41(1) assigns BMC constitution to the local body.
te: BMCs, SBB village field units కావు. Section 8 NBA establishmentను Central Governmentకు, section 22 SBB establishmentను State Governmentకు, section 41(1) BMC constitutionను local bodyకి assign చేస్తాయి.

en: A BMC is locally constituted and is not subordinate to an SBB; the three levels coordinate without forming a command chain. The Act also creates National, State and Local Biodiversity Funds. Charges, royalties and benefit-sharing receipts enter the relevant funds and finance legally assigned purposes so benefits can reach eligible claimers.
te: BMC localగా constitute అవుతుంది; SBBకు subordinate కాదు. Three levels command chainగా కాక coordinationతో పనిచేస్తాయి. Act National, State, Local Biodiversity Fundsను కూడా create చేస్తుంది. Charges, royalties, benefit-sharing receipts relevant Fundsలో చేరి legally assigned purposesకు finance ఇస్తాయి; benefits eligible claimersకు చేరేలా చేస్తాయి.

en: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 was renamed the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 in 2023. Forest land covered by the Act generally requires prior Central Government approval before non-forest use. The provision for areas within 100 km of an international border, LoC or LAC is not a blanket exemption: it applies only to strategic linear projects of national importance and concerning national security that satisfy the Act. Other exclusions for defence, security and notified Left-Wing Extremism-affected areas also have specific limits and conditions.
te: Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980కు 2023లో **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980** అనే పేరు వచ్చింది. ఈ law వర్తించే forest landను non-forest purposeకు ఉపయోగించే ముందు సాధారణంగా Central Government prior approval అవసరం. International border, Line of Control (LoC) లేదా Line of Actual Control (LAC) నుంచి 100 km పరిధిలో ఉందనే కారణంతో ప్రతి projectకు exemption రాదు. Actలో చెప్పిన conditionsను meet చేసే national importance లేదా national securityకు సంబంధించిన strategic linear projectకే ఆ provision వర్తిస్తుంది. Defence, security, Left-Wing Extremism-affected areasకు సంబంధించిన ఇతర exclusions కూడా limited conditionsతోనే ఉంటాయి.

en: After forest diversion is approved, the user agency generally pays the cost of compensatory afforestation and Net Present Value. These funds are managed for statutory purposes through the National Fund, State Funds and their CAMPA authorities under the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016. The Act replaced the earlier ad hoc arrangement created under Supreme Court directions with a permanent statutory framework.
te: Forest diversion approve అయిన తరువాత user agency సాధారణంగా compensatory afforestation cost, Net Present Value (NPV) చెల్లిస్తుంది. ఈ moneyని ordinary government revenueలా ఖర్చు చేయరు. Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016 ప్రకారం National Fund, State Funds మరియు వాటి CAMPA authorities statutory purposes కోసం manage చేస్తాయి. అంతకుముందు Supreme Court directions కింద ad hocగా ఉన్న CAMPA arrangementకు 2016 Act permanent statutory structure ఇచ్చింది.

en: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 recognises pre-existing rights of eligible Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers; it does not create a new charity. An Individual Forest Right relates to forest land occupied for habitation or self-cultivation, subject to the Act. A Community Forest Resource right enables the Gram Sabha or community to protect, regenerate, conserve, manage and sustainably use its customary forest resource. The Gram Sabha begins the claims process. In a Critical Wildlife Habitat, rights recognition and exclusion-based conservation can create conflict and must follow the statutory safeguards.
te: Forest Rights Act, 2006 కొత్తగా charity ఇవ్వదు; eligible Scheduled Tribes, Other Traditional Forest Dwellersకు గతం నుంచి ఉన్న rightsను recognise చేస్తుంది. Individual Forest Right (IFR) అనేది individual లేదా household నివసిస్తూ సాగు చేస్తున్న forest landతో సంబంధం కలిగి ఉంటుంది. Community Forest Resource (CFR) right ద్వారా Gram Sabha/community తన customary forest resourceను protect, regenerate, conserve, manage చేసి sustainably use చేయగలదు. Claims processను Gram Sabha ప్రారంభిస్తుంది. Critical Wildlife Habitatలో rights recognition, exclusion-based conservation మధ్య conflict రావచ్చు; రెండూ automaticగా harmonious అని భావించకూడదు.

en: Rule 5 of the Wetlands Rules, 2017 provides a Wetlands Authority for every State and Union Territory. In a State, the Minister in charge of environment, forests or wetlands is Chairperson and the Chief Secretary is Vice-Chairperson. In a Union Territory, the Administrator or Chief Secretary chairs it. This decentralised arrangement replaced the Central Wetlands Regulatory Authority under the 2010 Rules; there was no body called the National Wetland Regulatory Authority.
te: Wetlands Rules, 2017లో Rule 5 ప్రకారం ప్రతి State, Union Territoryకు Wetlands Authority ఉంటుంది. Stateలో environment, forests లేదా wetlands portfolio చూసే Minister Chairperson; Chief Secretary Vice-Chairperson. Union Territoryలో Administrator లేదా Chief Secretary chair చేస్తారు. ఈ decentralised system, 2010 Rulesలోని **Central Wetlands Regulatory Authority** స్థానంలో వచ్చింది. దాని పేరు ‘National Wetland Regulatory Authority’ కాదు.

en: A Ramsar Site has international recognition under the Convention on Wetlands. Notification and regulation under the Wetlands Rules, 2017 are separate domestic legal processes. A wetland may have either status, both, or neither; international designation and domestic restriction are not the same.
te: Ramsar Site అనేది Ramsar Convention కింద international recognition. Wetlands Rules, 2017 కింద notification, regulation మాత్రం domestic legal process. అందువల్ల ఒక wetlandకు Ramsar status మాత్రమే ఉండవచ్చు, domestic notification మాత్రమే ఉండవచ్చు, రెండూ ఉండవచ్చు లేదా రెండూ లేకపోవచ్చు. International label, domestic restriction ఒకటే కాదు.

en: The Wetlands Rules, 2017 are subordinate legislation under the Environment (Protection) Act. They prohibit or regulate specified activities in notified wetlands. The National Plan for Conservation of Aquatic Ecosystems is instead a Centrally Sponsored Scheme that supports lake and wetland conservation projects; it is not a statutory authority. It was formed in 2013 by merging the National Wetland Conservation Programme and National Lake Conservation Plan. MoEFCC states a funding pattern of 60:40 for States, 90:10 for North-Eastern States and 100% Central funding for Union Territories.
te: Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017 అనేవి Environment (Protection) Act కింద subordinate legislation. ఇవి notified wetlandsలో specified activitiesను prohibit లేదా regulate చేస్తాయి. National Plan for Conservation of Aquatic Ecosystems (NPCA) మాత్రం statutory authority కాదు; lakes, wetlands conservation projectsకు support ఇచ్చే Centrally Sponsored Scheme. National Wetland Conservation Programme, National Lake Conservation Planను merge చేసి 2013లో NPCAను ప్రారంభించారు. MoEFCC official funding statement ప్రకారం సాధారణ Statesకు Centre–State funding 60:40; North-Eastern Statesకు 90:10; Union Territoriesకు 100% Central funding.

en: CRZ and Eco-Sensitive Zones both derive authority from the Environment (Protection) Act, but regulate different landscapes. The CRZ Notification, 2019 classifies coastal areas and superseded the 2011 notification. An ESZ is a site-specific regulated belt around a protected area. The two instruments are not interchangeable.
te: CRZ, Eco-Sensitive Zone (ESZ) రెండూ Environment (Protection) Act నుంచి authority పొందినా, regulate చేసే landscape వేరు. CRZ Notification, 2019 coastను classify చేస్తుంది; అది 2011 notificationను replace చేసింది. ESZ మాత్రం protected area చుట్టూ site-specific regulated belt. ఒకే parent Act కింద ఉన్నాయనే కారణంతో CRZ, ESZను interchange చేయకూడదు.

en: Under the CRZ Notification, 2019, ecologically sensitive features fall in CRZ-I A and the inter-tidal zone in CRZ-I B. Developed urban coast is CRZ-II, while relatively undisturbed or rural coast is CRZ-III. The notified No Development Zone is 50 metres in densely populated CRZ-III A and 200 metres in CRZ-III B. Coastal and tidal-influenced waters fall in CRZ-IV. Questions should be answered using the category and threshold in the operative notification.
te: CRZ Notification, 2019లో ecologically sensitive features **CRZ-I A**లో, inter-tidal zone **CRZ-I B**లో ఉంటాయి. Developed urban coast **CRZ-II**; relatively undisturbed లేదా rural coast **CRZ-III**. Densely populated CRZ-III Aలో notified No Development Zone 50 metres; CRZ-III Bలో 200 metres. Coastal waters, tidal-influenced waters **CRZ-IV**లో వస్తాయి. Examలో operative notificationలోని category, thresholdనే ఉపయోగించాలి.

en: When a mangrove area exceeds 1,000 square metres, the CRZ Notification, 2019 places it in CRZ-I A and also includes the specified 50-metre buffer along the mangroves in CRZ-I A. The threshold and buffer should not be mechanically applied to every smaller mangrove patch.
te: Mangrove area 1,000 square metresకంటే ఎక్కువగా ఉంటే, CRZ Notification, 2019 దాన్ని CRZ-I Aగా classify చేస్తుంది; mangroves వెంట specified 50-metre bufferను కూడా CRZ-I Aలో చేర్చుతుంది. ఈ area threshold, bufferను ప్రతి చిన్న mangrove patchకు mechanically apply చేయకూడదు.

en: Do not confuse a statutory fund mechanism with an executive scheme. CAMPA has a statutory basis under the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016, whereas NPCA is a scheme. NGT jurisdiction is limited to enactments listed in Schedule I of the NGT Act, which does not include the Wild Life (Protection) Act. A wildlife dispute usually reaches the NGT only when it also raises a substantial environmental question under a listed law such as the Environment (Protection) Act, forest-conservation law or Biological Diversity Act.
te: Legal statusను schemeతో కలపకూడదు. CAMPAకు Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016 కింద statutory basis ఉంది; NPCA executive scheme. అలాగే NGT jurisdiction, NGT Act Schedule Iలో listed enactmentsకే పరిమితం. Wild Life (Protection) Act ఆ Scheduleలో లేదు. కాబట్టి wildlife disputeలో EPA, forest-conservation law, Biological Diversity Act వంటి listed lawకు సంబంధించిన substantial environmental question కూడా ఉన్నప్పుడే NGT route సాధారణంగా తెరుచుకుంటుంది.

en: India's environmental institutions do not exercise the same authority. NBWL advises and reviews; NTCA oversees tiger-reserve governance; NGT adjudicates specified disputes. Policy, regulation, administration, research, monitoring and adjudication should be separated. National importance alone does not make an institution statutory; legislation must create or authorise it.
te: Indiaలో environmental institutions అన్నీ ఒకే authorityను exercise చేయవు. NBWL advice, review చేస్తుంది; NTCA Tiger Reserve governanceను supervise చేస్తుంది; NGT specified disputesను adjudicate చేస్తుంది. Policy, regulation, administration, research, monitoring, adjudication అనే rolesను ముందుగా వేరు చేసి చదవాలి. ఒక institution national importance కలిగి ఉన్నంత మాత్రాన statutory body కాదు; legislation దాన్ని create లేదా authorise చేసినప్పుడే statutory status వస్తుంది.

en: MoEFCC is the Union Government's nodal ministry for environment, forests and wildlife. It frames central policy and supervises specialised bodies or receives their reports. It functions under the Allocation of Business Rules and is not an authority created by one environmental statute.
te: MoEFCC, environment, forests, wildlife విషయాల్లో Union Government nodal ministry. Central policyని frame చేసి, specialised bodiesను supervise చేస్తుంది లేదా వాటి reportsను receive చేస్తుంది. ఇది Allocation of Business Rules కింద పనిచేసే Ministry; ఒక particular environmental statute create చేసిన authority కాదు.

en: The National Biodiversity Authority in Chennai is a statutory body established by the Central Government under section 8 of the Biological Diversity Act. It regulates access by persons covered by section 3(2), oversees Access and Benefit-sharing arrangements and advises the Central Government.
te: Chennaiలోని National Biodiversity Authority (NBA), Biological Diversity Act section 8 కింద Central Government ఏర్పాటు చేసిన statutory body. Section 3(2) పరిధిలోని persons biological resources లేదా associated knowledgeను access చేసే సందర్భాలను regulate చేయడం, Access and Benefit-sharing (ABS) arrangementsను oversee చేయడం, Central Governmentకు advice ఇవ్వడం దీని ప్రధాన functions.

en: The National Board for Wild Life is the apex statutory advisory body under section 5A of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, with the Prime Minister as Chairperson. Its Standing Committee scrutinises proposals affecting protected areas when the applicable approval route requires it. Field authorities, not NBWL, conduct day-to-day protected-area management.
te: National Board for Wild Life (NBWL), WPA section 5A కింద ఉన్న apex statutory advisory body; Prime Minister దీనికి Chairperson. Protected areasను ప్రభావితం చేసే proposalsను applicable approval routeలో దాని Standing Committee scrutinise చేస్తుంది. NBWL advice, review చేస్తుంది; day-to-day protected-area management field authorities పని.

en: The National Tiger Conservation Authority is the statutory tiger-governance authority under section 38L of the Wild Life (Protection) Act. It oversees standards, tiger conservation plans and specified approvals for Tiger Reserves. It is distinct from WII's research role, NBWL's advisory role and wildlife funding schemes.
te: National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), WPA section 38L కింద statutory tiger-governance authority. Tiger Reservesకు standards, conservation plans, approvalsను oversee చేస్తుంది. ఇది WII research role కాదు; NBWL advisory role కాదు; wildlife funding scheme కూడా కాదు.

en: The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau coordinates intelligence and enforcement against organised wildlife crime. Section 38Y of the Wild Life (Protection) Act establishes this statutory Bureau; section 38XA is a savings provision, not its constituting section.
te: Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB), organised wildlife crimeపై intelligence, enforcement coordination చేస్తుంది. WPA section 38Y ఈ statutory Bureauను create చేసింది. Section 38XA savings provision మాత్రమే; WCCB constituting section కాదు.

en: The Central Zoo Authority recognises and regulates Indian zoos and sets zoo-management standards. Its work also includes ex-situ conservation, conservation breeding and Species Survival Plans. Section 38A, inserted by the 1991 amendment to the Wild Life (Protection) Act, gives it statutory status.
te: Central Zoo Authority (CZA), Indian zoosను recognise, regulate చేసి zoo-management standardsను set చేస్తుంది. Ex-situ conservation, conservation breeding, Species Survival Plans కూడా దీని workలో భాగం. 1991 Amendmentతో వచ్చిన WPA section 38A, CZAకు statutory basis ఇచ్చింది.

en: The Wildlife Institute of India in Dehradun is a national institution for wildlife research and training. It develops population-estimation and monitoring methods, supports management planning and maintains the National Wildlife Database. Established in 1982 and autonomous from April 1986, it is an autonomous MoEFCC institution rather than a statutory body.
te: Wildlife Institute of India (WII), Dehradun wildlife research, trainingకు national institution. Population-estimation, monitoring methodsను develop చేసి management planningకు support ఇస్తుంది; National Wildlife Databaseను maintain చేస్తుంది. 1982లో establish అయి April 1986 నుంచి autonomousగా పనిచేస్తున్న WII, MoEFCC autonomous institution; statutory body కాదు.

en: The Botanical Survey of India and Zoological Survey of India, both headquartered in Kolkata, survey, explore, classify and inventory plants and animals respectively. Their taxonomic work documents known diversity and helps identify previously unrecorded species. Both are non-statutory subordinate offices of MoEFCC.
te: Kolkataలోని Botanical Survey of India (BSI), Zoological Survey of India (ZSI) వరుసగా plants, animalsపై survey, exploration, classification, inventory చేస్తాయి. Taxonomic work ద్వారా known diversityను document చేసి, unrecorded speciesను identify చేయడంలో సహాయపడతాయి. రెండూ MoEFCC subordinate offices; statutory authorities కావు.

en: The Forest Survey of India in Dehradun monitors forest and tree resources through satellite forest-cover mapping, the National Forest Inventory and forest-fire alerts. Its flagship publication is the biennial India State of Forest Report. FSI was created on 1 June 1981 as successor to the Pre-Investment Survey of Forest Resources begun in 1965. It is a non-statutory subordinate office of MoEFCC.
te: Forest Survey of India (FSI), Dehradun satellite forest-cover mapping, National Forest Inventory, forest-fire alerts ద్వారా forest and tree resourcesను monitor చేస్తుంది. Biennial India State of Forest Report దీని flagship publication. 1965లోని Pre-Investment Survey of Forest Resourcesకు successorగా 1 June 1981న FSI ఏర్పడింది. ఇది non-statutory MoEFCC subordinate office.

en: ICAR–National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources in New Delhi is India's nodal institution for plant genetic resources. It collects, quarantines, characterises and evaluates germplasm and conserves it ex situ in the National Genebank. India's first National Genebank was established there in 1996; official ICAR information reported 0.47 million accessions and 12 regional stations as of 15 January 2025. Such operational totals are date-specific.
te: ICAR–National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources (NBPGR), New Delhi plant genetic resourcesకు nodal institution. Germplasm collection, quarantine, characterisation, evaluation చేసి, National Genebankలో ex-situగా conserve చేస్తుంది. India's first National Genebankను 1996లో ఇక్కడ establish చేశారు. ICAR official information ప్రకారం 15 January 2025 నాటికి 0.47 million accessions, 12 regional stations ఉన్నాయి. ఇవి date-specific operational figures.

en: SACON near Anaikatty, Coimbatore specialises in ornithology and natural history. It supports research on birds and habitats, ornithological information and postgraduate and doctoral training. SACON is an autonomous MoEFCC institution, not a statutory authority. National roles do not by themselves make FSI, NBPGR or SACON statutory.
te: Anaikatty, Coimbatore సమీపంలోని SACON, ornithology, natural historyలో specialise చేస్తుంది. en: The National Green Tribunal, established in 2010, is a specialised adjudicatory forum. It hears substantial environmental questions arising under the seven enactments listed in Schedule I of the NGT Act; it does not make policy or manage sites. Because the Wild Life (Protection) Act is not in Schedule I, a wildlife issue alone does not automatically confer jurisdiction; there must also be an overlapping issue under a listed enactment.
te: National Green Tribunal (NGT), 2010లో ఏర్పడిన specialised adjudicatory forum. NGT Act Schedule Iలోని seven enactments కింద వచ్చే substantial environmental questionsను hear చేస్తుంది. Policy తయారు చేయడం లేదా field management దీని పని కాదు. WPA Schedule Iలో లేకపోవడంతో wildlife issue మాత్రమే ఉన్న dispute automaticగా NGT jurisdictionలోకి రాదు; listed law కింద overlapping issue కూడా అవసరం.

en: National and State CAMPA bodies manage funds collected from forest diversion for compensatory afforestation and related restoration. The Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016 gave statutory form to the earlier ad hoc arrangement created under Supreme Court directions.

en: Protected-area totals must always carry a date. A PIB release of 3 March 2025 reproduced the National Wildlife Database snapshot of 27 November 2023: 106 National Parks, 573 Wildlife Sanctuaries, 115 Conservation Reserves and 220 Community Reserves, totalling 1,014 protected areas and 5.32% of India's geographical area. These figures are historical, not current; Tiger Reserve, Biosphere Reserve and Ramsar totals also change. This dated national share is not the same measure as the global 30×30 target.
te: Protected-area numbersను date లేకుండా quote చేయకూడదు. 3 March 2025 PIB release, National Wildlife Databaseలోని 27 November 2023 snapshotను reproduce చేసింది: 106 National Parks, 573 Wildlife Sanctuaries, 115 Conservation Reserves, 220 Community Reserves—మొత్తం 1,014 protected areas; India's geographical areaలో 5.32%. Tiger Reserve, Biosphere Reserve, Ramsar totals కూడా recognition మారినప్పుడల్లా మారతాయి. ఈ dated national percentage, global 30×30 target ఒకే measure కాదు.

en: India's biodiversity-planning sequence is: the 1999 macro-level strategy, Cabinet-approved NBAP 2008, the 2014 Addendum and NBSAP 2024–2030. India did not replace NBAP 2008 when the CBD adopted 20 Aichi Targets. The 2014 Addendum collectively incorporated those targets into 12 Indian National Biodiversity Targets; the mapping was not one-to-one.
te: India biodiversity-planning sequence: 1999 macro-level strategy → Cabinet-approved NBAP 2008 → 2014 Addendum → NBSAP 2024–2030. CBDలో 20 Aichi Targets వచ్చిన తరువాత India NBAP 2008ను replace చేయలేదు. 2014 Addendum, 12 Indian National Biodiversity Targetsలో మొత్తం 20 Aichi Targetsను collectively absorb చేసింది; mapping one-to-one కాదు.

en: India released NBSAP 2024–2030 at CBD COP16 in Cali on 30 October 2024. Its 23 National Biodiversity Targets align with the 23 targets of the KMGBF and use 2030 and 2050 horizons. India treats Target 3 as a collective global goal rather than an identical national quota; qualifying OECMs may contribute without becoming protected areas under the Wild Life (Protection) Act.
te: India, NBSAP 2024–2030ను 30 October 2024న Cali CBD COP16లో release చేసింది. ఇందులో 23 National Biodiversity Targets, KMGBFలోని 23 targetsతో align అవుతూ 2030, 2050 horizonsను ఉపయోగిస్తాయి. India, Target 3ను identical national quotaగా కాక collective global goalగా చూస్తుంది; qualifying OECMs, WPA protected areasగా మారకుండానే contribute చేయవచ్చు.

en: The Seventh National Report should be read as a dated Government self-assessment, not an independent evaluation. MoEFCC submitted it to the CBD on 26 February 2026. It uses 142 national indicators mapped to 23 National Biodiversity Targets and draws on coordinated inputs from ministries, States, statutory authorities and research institutions. SBBs support State-level implementation, while BMCs and People's Biodiversity Registers provide local evidence.
te: Seventh National Reportను dated Government self-assessmentగా చదవాలి; independent evaluationగా కాదు. MoEFCC ఈ reportను 26 February 2026న CBDకు submit చేసింది. ఇందులో 23 National Biodiversity Targetsకు map చేసిన 142 national indicators ఉన్నాయి; Ministries, States, statutory authorities, research institutions ఇచ్చిన coordinated inputsను ఉపయోగించింది. SBBs State-level implementationకు support చేస్తాయి; BMCs, People's Biodiversity Registers ద్వారా local evidenceను అందిస్తాయి.
